BiblicalUsage: Heth is the ancestor of the Hittites, a son of Canaan named in the table of nations, and his children become the people Israel must deal with for centuries. Abraham speaks to the sons of Heth when he buys the burial cave for Sarah, and the chronicler traces the same line in the genealogy of the nations.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the sons of Heth show how the nations around Israel were real neighbours with real claims, not faceless enemies. I hold that Abraham dealing fairly with them is a model for how God's people treat those outside the covenant.
